notes: Refined from the naive draft (3899 candidate entries, 3571 flagged FUZZY MATCH) using the same methodology as episodes 28-29. Core cast confirmed via clean exact/segment matches: Katarzyna Meciński, Hanna Zagulska, Daria Dąbrowska, Katina, Aniela Olszewska, Jakub Łysiak, Krzysztof Gonciarz, Konrad Krasuski, Weronika Truszczyńska, Magdalena Gwóźdź, Ewa Wyczółkowska, Krzysztof Stanowski, Tomasz Działowy, Szymon Adam Opolski, Julia Wieliczko. Ambiguous bare first names were resolved per-instance via context rather than blanket rule, since some names (Krzysztof, Hanna, Kuba) are shared by multiple real characters in this episode: every bare 'Krzysztof'/'Krzysztofa' found resolves to Krzysztof Gonciarz (id 1) -- Stanowski is always named with his surname when discussed; almost every bare 'Hanna'/'Hania'/'Hanny' resolves to Hanna Zagulska (id 10), except a single multi-line 'Hanny .../ Koczewskiej' at [01:18:28]/[01:18:32], the only genuine Hanna Koczewska reference in the whole episode; 'Kuba' at [02:34:43]/[02:42:55]/[26:46] resolves to Jakub Łysiak (id 8, alias 'Wąsik') via multi-line surname splits and shared storyline, even though the naive generator's candidate list for bare 'Kuba' never included id 8 (he has no bare 'Kuba' alias listed) -- these three were added as missed mentions. Two false positives were dropped: 'Jezus Maria' at [01:13:40] (idiom, not a Maria mention) and 'maja 16' at [43:18] (the month of May, not Maja Mikołajczyk/Staśko). One case was excluded rather than guessed: an unidentified 'Marcin' at [01:31:18] who translated a post, with no surname or other context pointing to any of the three candidate Marcin entities. Two low-confidence ambiguous cases remain flagged in-line: 'Michał' at [00:53]/[00:55] in a chaotic fast-cut intro montage (assigned to generic 'Michał', id 82, as the most neutral guess), and 'Ola' at [02:34:48]/[02:35:23] (assigned to Olciak, id 35, for consistency with the same unresolved case in earlier episodes). As before, the large majority of the 3571 FUZZY MATCH candidates were common Polish words coincidentally close in edit-distance to a name (e.g. 'jak'->Jakub, 'masz'->Tomasz, 'Polska/polski'->Opolski, 'sylwestra' [New Year's Eve, genitive]-> Sylwester Wardenga) and were discarded; only genuine inflections/ASR-typos of names actually discussed here were kept.
